output.title: What contact decay hides in a small business
output.body:
Contact decay is not usually a grand strategy problem. In a 1-10 person business, it is the quiet moment when a lead, customer, or supplier contact goes stale and nobody notices until the opportunity has already slipped. That can happen in a CRM, an inbox, or a spreadsheet with tidy columns and no follow-up discipline. The real issue is visibility: if you do not know which contacts have gone quiet, you do not know whether you have a sales problem, a process problem, or just a memory problem. Human memory is a brave little filing system, but it is not a system.

The bounded workflow decision is simple: first check whether your contacts already live in a digital tool where silence can be seen at a glance. If they do, a lightweight flag for dormant contacts may be worth building later. If most contacts arrive by phone call or walk-in, AI is probably not the right fit.

The practical next step is manual. Take one week of your contact list and mark every record you know has gone dormant. Then write down how you noticed each one: missed reply, old quote, customer who never came back, or a note you found too late. Once you can see which contacts have gone quiet and why, you will know whether this is a real workflow cost or just background noise.
